issues.legal_issue: An oral agreement to sell co-owners’ shares in land was established by the evidence.
material_facts: The prospective buyer and the selling co-owners were found to have agreed orally on a sale of their shares.
Several witnesses corroborated that the co-owners agreed to sell at a fixed price.
Most of the selling co-owners later executed sale deeds to the buyer at that price, and other co-owners sold at the same price to the competing purchaser.
The buyer had built a cinema building on the site and had been negotiating to purchase it for several years.
issues.conclusion: The finding that the oral agreement to sell the shares was made was affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: Whether an oral agreement was made is determined from the evidence and circumstances as a whole. The corroborating testimony and subsequent sales at the agreed price supported the finding that an agreement had been concluded.

predicates.oral_sale_dispute: The proceeding concerns a claimed oral agreement to sell interests in land.
predicates.corroborated_agreement_evidence: Witnesses other than the claimed buyer gave evidence supporting that the sellers agreed to the sale.
predicates.subsequent_sales_at_agreed_price: Some sellers later conveyed their interests at the price said to have been agreed.

issues.definition: When a dispute over an oral land sale is supported by corroborating evidence and subsequent sales at the agreed price, the oral sale agreement is established.

issues.legal_issue: An oral land-sale agreement can bind the parties despite an unexecuted formal document and an unsettled mode of payment when the parties intended to be bound and its vital terms were fixed.
material_facts: The parties agreed orally on the price, the area of land, and the time for completing the sale.
They contemplated that a written agreement would be prepared later, but the evidence did not show that signing it was a prerequisite to the oral agreement taking effect.
The parties did not specifically agree on the mode of payment.
issues.conclusion: The oral agreement was not ineffective merely because no formal written agreement was executed or the mode of payment was not settled.
issues.legal_principle: A future formal document does not prevent an existing binding bargain unless the parties intended its execution to be a condition of being bound. Whether it was a condition depends on intention and the circumstances. The omission of a mode of payment does not necessarily make a contract incomplete where its vital terms are fixed. The Court relied on Ridgway v. Wharton, Von Hatzfeldt-Wildenburg v. Alexander, Rossiter v. Miller, and Currimbhoy and Company Ltd. v. Creet.

rule.if: oral_land_sale_dispute and vital_sale_terms_fixed and formal_writing_not_condition and payment_method_unsettled

predicates.oral_land_sale_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether an oral agreement to sell land is binding.
predicates.vital_sale_terms_fixed: The parties settled the price, the land to be sold, and the time for completing the sale.
predicates.formal_writing_not_condition: The parties contemplated a later written document but did not make its execution a condition of being bound.
predicates.payment_method_unsettled: The parties did not settle how the purchase money would be paid.

issues.definition: In an oral land-sale dispute, an agreement remains binding despite an unsettled payment method and contemplated formal writing when its vital terms are fixed and the writing was not a condition of being bound.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser who had notice of a prior agreement to sell cannot establish that the purchase was made without notice.
material_facts: The competing purchaser acquired the shares after the prior oral agreement had been made.
Witnesses testified that they approached the purchaser after the agreement and asked him to sell his shares to the buyer under that agreement.
The purchaser did not deny meeting those witnesses, and the evidence supported the finding that he had notice of the prior agreement.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser failed to establish that he was a purchaser for value without notice of the prior agreement.
issues.legal_principle: A purchaser’s claim to have acquired property without notice of a prior agreement is assessed on the evidence of the purchaser’s knowledge at the time of purchase. The Court upheld the finding of notice on the evidence and found no reason to differ from the High Court.

predicates.specific_performance_dispute: The proceeding includes a claim to specifically enforce an earlier agreement to sell property.
predicates.purchase_after_prior_agreement: The competing purchaser acquired an interest in the property after the earlier agreement was made.
predicates.purchaser_had_notice: The purchaser knew of the earlier agreement when acquiring the interest.

issues.definition: In a specific-performance dispute, a purchaser who acquires property after an earlier agreement and has notice of it is not a purchaser without notice.

issues.legal_issue: Without an application invoking the statutory power, a court cannot direct that a particular portion of property be allotted to a co-owner in a partition.
material_facts: The dispute included a partition proceeding.
No application was made under section 2 of the Partition Act.
The High Court directed that, as far as possible, the portion of the site occupied by the buyer’s cinema building be allotted to him.
issues.conclusion: The direction to allot the particular portion had to be deleted because no application had been made under section 2 of the Partition Act; equitable directions could still be considered when making the final partition decree.
issues.legal_principle: In a partition proceeding, section 2 of the Partition Act did not empower the court to direct the allotment of a particular portion in the absence of an application under that section. The Court also referred to Rama Prasada Rao v. Subbaramaiah, while leaving open the making of equitable directions in the final partition decree.

predicates.partition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns division of property among co-owners.
predicates.no_application_for_statutory_partition_p: No party applied for the statutory power that would permit the court to make the relevant allotment direction.

issues.definition: In a partition proceeding, when no party applies for the statutory partition power, the court cannot direct that a particular portion be allotted to a co-owner.
